convoLines.text: "Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
"I don't talk about that. Not because it's secret — because saying it out loud makes it real in a way I can't afford yet. Someday. Not today."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on who you left behind."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. You don't know what it's like, being the only nobody in a camp of somebodies." Quiet. Real.
"That again?" Robin sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"See how Brazil Nuts grows — low, where the damp holds. That's the first thing to learn about it."
"When you reach a ridge with a view for miles, look for the high ground first. That's how you find your way back."
"So — That we're interesting to it. Being watched means being kept. I'd rather be boring to the sky. Boring things get left alone."
"Still on what scares you most. Don't waste it."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Jorge is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Adjeley grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Adjeley is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving. ...never mind."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on your read on people here."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Jorge owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I write everything down. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
"Wild Black Cherry. Remember the leaf, the stem, the smell — that's the whole of it."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on the kindest thing someone's done for you."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Jorge always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Nobody says Jorge's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Adjeley is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"I greet everyone by name each morning for Jorge, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 8 days back. Still on your mind? 'Alright — I should get back to it.'"
"Give it three more days of arguing. Then someone says the obvious thing and we all pretend it was theirs."
"My vote? I'm keeping it to myself until the shouting stops."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"Wild Carrot — the root's the honest part. Dig a little and you'll know it anywhere."
"See how Lantana grows — low, where the damp holds. That's the first thing to learn about it."
"Being a farmer taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew."
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." You give a lot of orders for someone nobody elected. I'm keeping track. So are others.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Adjeley nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Leadership is mostly listening, then deciding. People forget the listening part."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Water's almost gone — 6 liters. I can't carry enough alone. First light, the creek, you and me?"
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 6 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
You need to be right next to your partner, same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the creek water run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 0 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"I keep my eyes down when I pass it. Respect, maybe. Fear, probably. Both."
"We should talk about what we'd ask for. Before it asks first."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"And... scene. Good talk."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"Listen — I get it. Solitude's a resource too. Scarcer than food, some days."
"I go to the treeline edge and count my breaths. Ten of them. That's my alone. Then I come back — alone is a luxury, and also a little bit a lie."
"Still on needing to be alone."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Oliver always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Sleep's gone strange. I do push-ups at dawn at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Claire nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Nobody says Oliver's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you're still figuring everyone out. Figure anything out yet? Anyone you're watching?"
Robin has an edge today — something curdled.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
The moment passes without landing. Not yet.
"Go ahead — you've got my attention."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Oliver killed the things that come at night. I did too. That's a small club, and it's smaller now."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.

"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
Maya has an edge today — something curdled.
"This is Cassava. The leaf tells you the season, the stem tells you the ground. Learn both."
"Common Sorrel. Remember the leaf, the stem, the smell — that's the whole of it."
"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
"Take your time."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Yeah — Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"Still on that question. I mean it."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"Good question." Watch — I'll get a real laugh out of this camp before the week is out.
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I be honest? It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing. Trust me. Mostly."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Robin is gone, Eurico is gone, and Emma is gone. The fire doesn't care. That's what gets me — the fire doesn't care."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."

"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

d18: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d18: 🕯️ Jorge Zamora is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d18: What Jorge kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d18: "Jorge's gone." Adjeley looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Jorge." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d18: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Oliver blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d18: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d18: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d18: 📖 LEARNED: Anatomy (Level 1). You know where the important bits are. Arteries, joints, organs. Useful for healing or hurting.
d18: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d18: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.
d18: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d18: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d18: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d18: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Jorge Zamora, 18 days. The mantle passes to Oliver Choi.
d18: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Oliver Choi, 32 — a paramedic. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Beard Moss, Berserker Rage, Green Thumb, Literally.
d18: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Gardener of the Living Garden." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d18: The village's quarrel was with Jorge — and Jorge is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d18: At the grave, Robin, Adjeley, Katarina speak for Oliver — "Jorge trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d18: The fire knew Oliver before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
